title: Markets Get Ready For Black Friday And Retail-Heavy Weekend
text:
Shutterstock photo Wednesday, November 21, 2018, 11:52 AM, EST NASDAQ Composite +1.75% Dow +0.82% S&P 500 +1.12% Russell 2000 +1.59% NASDAQ Advancers: 1875 Decliners: 413 Today's Volume (vs yesterday) -34.5% Crude $54.40 +$0.97 Gold $1227.70 +$6.50 , VIX 20.98 -1.50 Market Movers
Consumer and Retail names rallying post earnings and guidance into Black Friday FAANG names bounce to lead major indexes higher Durable Goods Orders fall 4.4%, worse report in 15 months MBA Mortgage Applications fell 0.1% from last week Initial Jobless Claims rose to 224,000 claims, still near historic lows Continuing Jobless Claims were worse than expected at 1.668 million claims Michigan November Consumer Sentiment fall slightly to 97.5 from 98.3 in October Oil rallying after 7 weeks of declines Chris's Commentary
Tech stocks are leading the market higher as the FAANG names try to climb out of bear market territory. The sharp decline from their 52 week highs have helped create multiple volatile trading sessions that have ultimately lead all the major indexes lower since October. Negative sentiment continues to dominate trading, but the oversold condition in these names and thus the markets overall appear to be abating in the near term (FB +2.5%, AAPL + 0.75%, AMZN +2.4%, NFLX + 0.75% and GOOGL +1.75%).
Currently 8 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are trading higher with Consumer Discretionary and the newly minted Communications sectors both up over 1.7%. Crude rallies 2.5% after declining over 6% yesterday. Gold trade higher while the Dollar trades lower. The yield on the 10-yr now stands at 3.0737%.
Black Friday traditionally has been the day after Thanksgiving that marked the beginning of the Christmas shopping season for U.S. consumers. This shopping "holiday" can draw its roots back to 1924 when Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade made its debut (originally called Macy's Christmas Day Parade). The term Black Friday was coined in the 60's to refer to the time-period when retailers moved from "in the red" or loss to "black" meaning a profit for the year. Black Friday has grown to a bigger window over the years. Originally with early bird shopping specials on the day after Thanksgiving, to opening on Thanksgiving night, to deep discounts and highly promotional online sales over the entire weekend. Thus, Black Friday in no longer the one day, all-important indicator it use to be but a 5 day shopping extravaganza. The National Retail Federations (NRF) expects more than 164 million people to shop over the long weekend. "Whether it's heading to the stores after finishing their turkey or going online on Cyber Monday, consumers will be shopping all weekend and retailers will be ready to meet the demand," said NRF CEO Matt Shay. "Retail is a vibrant, dynamic and competitive industry, but one thing is certain - consumers are the winners no matter which day or which way they shop."
The Plymouth Colony celebrated Thanksgiving for the 1st time in 1621 and has been celebrated by many since. Abraham Lincoln made Thanksgiving an official holiday in the U.S. in 1862. Similar to then, we give thanks to family, friends and those who came before us. As Shakespeare once wrote, "O Lord that lends me life, lend me a heart replete with thankfulness." Happy Thanksgiving.

Brian's Technical Take
Yesterday we highlighted the bullish divergences present amongst the major equity indices represented by momentum measures which are making higher lows, the improving percentage of stocks trading above their 50-day moving average, and the declining percentage of stocks making new 52-week lows. The Nasdaq 100 and Composite are the only indices to make new lows in November vs. October and thus the others may need to follow suit before a longer lasting, intermediate term relief rally takes hold. Given Nasdaq's leadership role throughout this bull market, our indices may be a proper barometer to look to for the next direction.
The Nasdaq 100 (NDX) is one of the worst performing indices in Q4 with a decline of 14.4%, but it remains the top performer in 2018 with a YTD gain of 3.5%. At this week's low it came within 0.5% of the weekly closing low from Q1, and less than 5% from this year's intraday low. The point is that it is entering major horizontal support based on the prior lows of 2018. Usually when an instrument tests major support for the first time, that support holds and a relief rally follows. This expected support level is reinforced by an even greater trend seen on the long term monthly period chart. The trend line connecting the Great Recession lows of 2009 and the global bear market lows of Q1 2016 is now in play and being tested with the latest decline in November. This clustering of technical support amidst growing bullish divergences and positive seasonal forces suggests a rally may not be far off.
